subject: College season is here + taper secrets unlocked
preheader: The CSL is live, early dual meets are in the books, and your Monday set is ready.
heroHeading: Good morning swimmers and happy Monday
heroTeaser: The College Swimming League has officially tipped off, and Night Swim's Elvis Burroughs and Dax Hill joined SwimSwam to break down whether the first two matches lived up to the hype.
outroLine: That's the week in the water. Happy swimming,

workout.dateLabel: Mon, Sep 28 · distance freestyle threshold in the pool, core and stability on land

swimSet.title: Today's Swim Set
swimSet.description: A 3,050-yard aerobic builder focused on holding controlled threshold pace across longer freestyle efforts to train your body to sustain speed under fatigue.

lift.title: Today's Lift
lift.description: An anti-rotation stability and rotational power session targeting the core with a freestyle and backstroke emphasis to build the steady platform your stroke depends on.

newsItems.title: Night Swim breaks down the CSL's opening matches
newsItems.body: Elvis Burroughs and Dax Hill, the duo known as Night Swim, joined the SwimSwam Breakdown podcast to dissect the first two matches of the new College Swimming League. Worth a listen if you want the inside read on how the debut actually went.

newsItems.title: You can't out-taper bad recovery habits
newsItems.body: A sharp piece from Olivier Poirier-Leroy on SwimSwam makes the case that taper is only as good as the recovery you've built before it starts. If your body is already in a hole when taper kicks off, all the rest in the world won't dig you out.

newsItems.title: Florida women go 14-for-14 to open the season
newsItems.body: University of Florida women's swimming won every single event in their season opener against Vanderbilt, finishing 206 to 55. That's the kind of statement meet that sets a tone for the whole year.

newsItems.title: South Africa's Short Course Worlds roster is taking shape
newsItems.body: Several South African swimmers punched potential tickets to the World Short Course Championships on the final day of the 2026 South African Short Course Championships. A reminder that the international calendar is already moving fast.

athlete.name: Caeleb Dressel
athlete.photoCredit: Photo: JD Lasica from Pleasanton, CA, US, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
athlete.bio:
Caeleb Dressel is an American competitive swimmer born on August 16, 1996, in Green Cove Springs, Florida. He specializes in freestyle, butterfly, and individual medley events. He attended Clay High School and later swam collegiately at the University of Florida, where he is widely regarded as one of the greatest sprinters in swimming history.

Dressel is a nine-time Olympic gold medalist, including five golds at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics. He won a record seven gold medals at the 2017 World Aquatics Championships and holds world records in the 100 meter butterfly and 100 meter individual medley. He also won NCAA titles in the 50 yard freestyle, 100 yard freestyle, and 100 yard butterfly.
